limitations: No candidate target has been generated into a dataset or manually certified readable. Existing visibility flags cannot catch source text overlap.
Repeated gates of the same physical part are deduplicated by the parser BOM; repeated equal values on distinct parts remain independent targets.
Family/source split isolation was checked using train against validation/test family IDs; no validation/test labels were used to select candidate values.
All visible components introduce part numbers, connector labels, capacitor ratings, and qualified values in addition to resistances. A literal-value scorer must preserve those distinctions.
Count balancing alone cannot repair incorrect source labels or unreadable raster text; inspect representative training candidates before generating a new versioned snapshot.
recommendations: If generating, use training-only single-question value-reading rows for every eligible distinct part to diversify targets, retaining per-part source/image provenance and the existing frozen validation/test sets.
Keep native grounding/refusal supervision represented. Avoid merely duplicating the same first-two-resistor questions.

Choose board/value sampling caps from this training inventory so large boards and frequent capacitor/resistor values do not dominate; document the deterministic weighting rather than silently duplicating rows.

For a reviewable first expanded variant, compare deterministic caps of one or two targets per (training board, exact literal value); counts are recorded below. Select refdes representatives by a seeded rotation, and retain unique qualifiers/part-number labels. A cap reduces repeated equal values without using validation or heldout frequencies.
For development lookup sampling and smoke checks, select only from these 87 training families. Keep the frozen validation/test outputs out of sampled training questions and selection weights.
